newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MADDUX NEAR PERFECT AS BRAVES BEAT GIANTS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MADDUX NEAR PERFECT AS BRAVES BEAT GIANTS.

text.p: Four-time Cy Young Award winner Greg Maddux was perfect for better than half a game on Saturday and when he faltered Andruw Jones homered in the ninth to lead the Atlanta Braves to a 5-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
Maddux pitched perfect ball for 5 2/3 innings, retiring the first 17 batters he faced before allowing a two-out single in the sixth to pitcher Mark Gardner.

"I give up over 200 hits a year, so what's one more?" joked Maddux, who gave up two runs on a two-run homer by Glenallen Hill in the eighth that tied the game. He allowed just those two hits with one walk and six strikeouts over eight innings.
Jones, who came into the game defensively in the eighth, snapped the 2-2 tie with a solo homer off reliever Doug Henry (2-2) and Kenny Lofton added a two-run triple in a three-run ninth.
"We played them tough in both games but gave up big ninth innings," said Giants manager Dusty Baker said.
In Montreal, Carlos Perez pitched his second consecutive shutout and F.P. Santangelo homered twice and had four RBI as the Montreal Expos blanked the Chicago Cubs 5-0.
Perez (6-4), who shut out the Mets last Monday, went the distance, scattering seven hits.

Santangelo drove in a run with a ground out in the two-run third inning. He then lined a 3-2 pitch over the fence in left for a two-run homer off Cubs starter Terry Mulholland in the fifth and added a solo shot in the eighth off Mel Rojas.
Mulholland (5-5) who entered the game with a 13-3 lifetime record against the Expos, suffered the loss. He went six innings, allowing four runs and five hits.

In Cincinnati, Terry Pendleton had run-scoring doubles in a three-run fifth inning and a four-run seventh and Mike Kelly added a two-run homer to lead the Reds to a 10-5 thumping of the New York Mets.
Pendleton went 3-for-5 with three runs scored and Hal Morris added two hits and two RBI to lead a season-high 16-hit Reds attack.
Scott Sullivan (1-1) relieved an injured Mike Morgan and allowed one run over 3 2/3 innings to earn his first major league win. Cory Lidle (3-1) took the loss for New York.
At Colorado, Jeff Conine's two-run homer off Darren Holmes with one out in seventh inning rallied the Florida Marlins past the Rockies, 7-5.
Conine, whose two-run shot gave Florida a 6-5 lead, three hits and three RBI. Gregg Zaun added three hits and drove in a run for the Marlins.
Colorado lost despite a four-run first inning in which Larry Walker, Andres Galarraga, and Dante Bichette hit consecutive home runs.
Felix Heredia (3-0) picked up the win with two scoreless innings of relief. Darren Holmes (2-1) gave up two runs and five hits over four innings for the loss.
In Los Angeles, Hideo Nomo notched his first complete game of the season and Mike Piazza had three hits, including a homer, as the Dodgers beat the St Louis Cardinals 5-2.
Nomo (6-5), who carried a shutout into the ninth, allowed six hits and struck out 10 in snapping a career-high three-game losing streak.
Piazza had an RBI single in the first and capped a three-run third with his 10th homer.
Cardinals starter Danny Jackson (1-2) suffered the loss, allowing four runs and nine hits in four innings.
In Pittsburgh, Jon Lieber allowed two runs and five hits in six-plus innings and Joe Randa and Dale Sveum each drove in two runs as the Pirates pounded the philadelphia Phillies 9-2.
Lieber (3-7) walked one and struck out four. Matt Ruebel, Clint Sodowsky, Ricardo Rincon and Dave Wainhouse combined to pitch three hitless innings of relief to seal the win.
The Pirates snapped a 2-2 tie with a pair of runs in the fourth and padded the lead with five runs in the seventh.
Ryan Nye (0-1), who was making his major-league debut, surrendered four runs, six hits and four walks with one strikeout in 3 2/3 innings for the loss.
In San Diego, Scott Livingstone's pinch-hit single with two outs in the bottom of the 10th inning scored Tony Gwynn to lift the Padres to a 5-4 win over the Houston Astros.
Ramon Garcia (2-4) loaded the bases on two walks and a single to Wally Joyner. Livingstone, who hit for pitcher Trevor Hoffman, lined an 0-2 pitch into left field for the winning hit.
Hoffman (3-3) worked two scoreless innings of relief to earn the win.
Gwynn hit his 100th career home run in the the third inning to extend his hitting streak to 17 games.
